narr: A very moist (PWATs 2.0+ inches) and unstable (MLCAPE 2000-3000 J/KG) air mass led to be a very conducive environment for vigorous thunderstorm activity across portions of southwest Arizona. A cluster of thunderstorms developed near Yuma during the mid-afternoon hours leading to flash flooding and damaging winds across the Fortuna Hills area. Thereafter, additional storm complexes developed during the late afternoon and evening hours across portions of Yuma and La Paz Counties, likely due to the combination of terrain lift as well as colliding outflows from the storms that developed earlier in the afternoon across portions of Imperial and Riverside Counties.
ev: US-95 near Milepost 69 was flooded. Timing estimated from radar. No damages or injuries were reported.

Separate social media videos showed water from Fortuna Wash flowing over S Ave 14 1/2 E and E 48th Street, causing the streets to become impassable. Most of the rain, estimated around 1 to 2 inches fell over the headwaters of Fortuna Wash, 3 to 5 miles to the southeast of Fortuna Foothills. No damages or injuries were reported.
Flooding was reported on SR-72, west of McVay Road. No damages or injuries were reported.
Report from La Paz County Emergency Management of water rushing into houses. Washes in the area were running full. Timing estimated from radar. No injuries were reported.
